Carry item 3 itself dissolved into the deletion: the misleading message went out with the mechanism. ROUND N+1 then ran on the REVERTED subset -- doctrine, because a revert leaves the shipped half reviewed by nobody -- and returned 7 findings, 6 folded. Two were canary cases my revert had taken as collateral and which carried NONE of the escalation's defect: the CONFIG pairing case (PREFIX_SAMPLE['/event/'] > MIN_EVENT_PAGES, pure arithmetic over two module constants, killed on BOTH edges: sample 4->3 and floor 3->4) and a case pinning WHICH arm a thrown fetch reports on (the old case counted failures+warns===1, true under either arm; killed by swapping the arms). Note round 1 and round N+1 DISAGREED about the pairing case -- round 1 killed it for claiming a run has slack, round N+1 asked for it back; adjudicated by re-adding it with an honest label (it proves the constants are written with a gap, NOT that a run has slack, since real supply is min(distinct locs in window, 4)). Also folded: my cited evidence for the slack was a transient on /organisers/cumbaye, which is NOT an event page and cost a different floor entirely -- the comment now says the event-floor case is projected from the mechanism, not observed.
